title: feat: add a dashboard selector to the observability header
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Grafana is embedded in kiosk mode, so its own navigation is hidden and only the default dashboard was reachable. The other four current dashboards had no entry point.

- Adds a dashboard picker to the header, next to the theme toggle
- Builds the list from Grafana's search API, filtered to dashboards provisioned at the top level, so the `legacy/` folder stays out of the menu and there is no second catalogue to maintain
- Mirrors the selection into `?d=<uid>` so a dashboard link is shareable and survives a refresh
- Keys the iframe so switching adds one browser history entry instead of two
- Falls back to the current default dashboard if the list cannot be loaded

No Worker, provisioning or auth changes. Verified against a local Grafana: switching, deep links, back navigation, light mode and the accessible name.

gist.headline: Five dashboards, one door
gist.blurb: The observability nook grew a proper dashboard picker. Polli can now hop between Grafana views without memorizing secret kiosk-mode routes.
gist.summary: Added a Grafana dashboard selector to the observability header that loads top-level provisioned dashboards from Grafana search, stores the selected dashboard UID in ?d=<uid>, and falls back to the default dashboard if loading fails.
gist.impact: Observability operators can switch among all current top-level dashboards, share deep links, refresh safely, and use browser back navigation without Grafana's hidden kiosk navigation.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy observability control room: Polli, wearing tiny operator headphones, chooses among five labeled dashboard cards on a lime-green CRT terminal while a small garden of code-plants grows beside it. The selector represents the newly accessible dashboard catalogue and the linked map pin represents shareable ?d=<uid> deep links.
